threads.thread_goal: Align on current pain points and approve target tax workflow scope.

messages.text:
Good morning team. We're kicking off the Standardised Tax Documentation & Filing Workflow Rollout project today. The goal is to design and roll out a standardised, audit-ready tax documentation and filing workflow across departments before the next quarterly tax filing deadline—that's 21 days from now.

We need to map current processes, identify pain points, and agree on the scope of what we'll standardise. I'll be coordinating this effort, and we'll be working closely with tax and accounting teams.

Let's start by understanding where we are today. What are the biggest bottlenecks you're seeing in the current tax documentation and filing process?

Thanks for the kickoff. From my perspective, the main issue is that each department submits tax data in different formats. Finance sends spreadsheets one way, operations another way entirely. By the time it reaches the tax team, there's always rework and clarification requests. We lose days just standardising the inputs.
I'd add that we don't have a clear calendar or tracker for what's due when. Sometimes documents arrive late, and we scramble to meet filing deadlines. A centralised tracker would help a lot.
Yes, the format issue is real. I've been handling some of the reconciliation, and it takes time. Also, I'm not always sure who's responsible for what step. Sometimes things fall through the cracks.

That's exactly what we need to fix. So the pain points are: (1) inconsistent data formats across departments, (2) no centralised tracker or calendar, (3) unclear roles and responsibilities. Let me propose we start by mapping the current end-to-end process—T1 covers this. We'll interview key contacts in accounting, finance, and operations to document how things flow today, identify bottlenecks, and then design the target state.

For scope, I suggest we focus on the core tax filing cycle: quarterly and annual filings. We can expand later if needed. Does that sound reasonable?
Agreed. Quarterly and annual is the right scope to start. That covers the bulk of our work. I can help with the interviews—I know the contacts in most departments.
Makes sense. Once we have the map, we'll need to define who does what at each step. That's where the RACI matrix comes in—T4. I can help review that once it's drafted.

Good. So here's what I'm thinking: I'll own the workflow map (A1) and the RACI matrix (A5). I'll coordinate the interviews, draft the map, and then we'll review it together. Does that work for everyone?
Yes, that works. I can support with the interviews if you need me to.
Perfect. I'll start scheduling the interviews with finance and operations contacts this week. Should we aim to have the draft map ready by end of week?

Yes, end of week is the target. That gives us time to review and refine before we move to template design. Let me confirm the scope decision: we're standardising quarterly and annual tax filing processes across accounting, finance, and operations departments. Agreed?
Agreed.
Confirmed.
Yes, that's clear.

Great. So to summarise: D1 is locked—scope is quarterly and annual tax filings across accounting, finance, and operations. D2 is locked—I'll own the workflow map and RACI matrix. Next steps: interviews this week, draft map by EOW, then we move to template design. Let's reconvene in this thread once the map is ready for review.

threads.thread_goal: Design and sign off templates, tracker, and checklist for tax documentation.

messages.text:
Hi team. I've drafted the first set of standard templates for tax-relevant documents. I've created templates for invoices summary, deductions, and adjustments—the three main data types we need to collect from departments.

I've also cross-checked them against current tax legislation to make sure we're capturing all required fields. The templates are in the shared folder. Can you review and let me know if anything is missing or unclear?

Thanks for getting these drafted quickly. I'll review them today. In parallel, I've been thinking about the tracker structure. We need a centralised spreadsheet that shows document status, owner, and due dates. Let me sketch out what I'm thinking:

- Document name
- Department owner
- Status (pending, submitted, reviewed, approved)
- Due date
- Actual submission date
- Notes

Does this cover what we need, or should we add more fields?

That looks good. I'd add one more field: 'Assigned to' so we know who in the department is responsible for submitting. Sometimes the department owner is a manager, but the actual person doing the work is different.
Good point. Also, should we have a field for the filing deadline? So people know when the document needs to be ready by?

Yes, that's already in 'Due date'. But I can make the label clearer—'Tax filing deadline' instead of just 'Due date'. Good catch. So the updated tracker fields are:

- Document name
- Department owner
- Assigned to (individual contact)
- Status
- Tax filing deadline
- Actual submission date
- Notes

I'll build this out in a spreadsheet and lock the structure so it doesn't get accidentally modified. We'll also need to define access rules—who can edit what.

That structure looks solid. Now, back to the templates—I want to make sure they're clear enough for non-finance staff to use. I've included examples of correct and incorrect entries, but I'm wondering if we should also create a quick-reference checklist. Something like 'Before you submit, check that you've included X, Y, Z.'

Absolutely. That's the pre-filing checklist—A4. We can create one for each document type. I'll draft those once the templates are finalised. Let me review your templates today and get back to you with feedback by EOD tomorrow.
While you're reviewing, should we also think about how departments will actually submit these documents? Email? Shared folder? The tracker?

Good question. I think the tracker should be the single source of truth. Departments upload documents to a shared folder linked in the tracker, and they update the status in the tracker when they submit. That way everything is in one place and we avoid duplicate files or lost emails.
That makes sense. So the tracker is the hub. I can help set up the folder structure and access permissions once we finalise the tracker design.
Sounds good. I'll wait for feedback on the templates, then we can move to approval. Once the templates are locked, we can also create the checklists and guidelines.

Let me confirm the tracker structure decision: we're going with document name, department owner, assigned to, status, tax filing deadline, actual submission date, and notes. All documents go to a shared folder, and the tracker is the single source of truth. Agreed?
Agreed. And I'll have the template feedback to you by tomorrow EOD so we can move to approval.
Confirmed on the tracker structure.

Perfect. So D3 and D4 are locked: templates approved (pending final review), and tracker structure confirmed. Next steps: I'll review templates by tomorrow EOD, we'll incorporate feedback, and then move to approval by the accounting department representative. T2 and T3 should be complete by mid-week.

threads.thread_goal: Lock roles, responsibilities, and reminder/escalation rules.

messages.text:
Team, I've drafted the RACI matrix for the new tax workflow. This clarifies who is responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed at each step of the process.

I've mapped out the key steps: data collection, document review, tax calculation, filing, and post-filing. For each step, I've assigned roles based on the workflow map we created earlier.

I've also drafted a reminder and escalation plan to make sure we don't miss deadlines. The idea is to send reminders at T-14 days, T-7 days, and T-3 days before each filing deadline. If a department hasn't submitted by T-3 days, we escalate to their manager.

Can you review both and let me know if the roles make sense and if the reminder schedule is realistic?

I've reviewed the RACI. It looks mostly right, but I have a question: for the 'tax calculation' step, you have me as responsible and the finance manager as accountable. But in practice, I often need input from finance on specific line items. Should finance be 'consulted' rather than just 'informed'?

Good catch. Yes, finance should be 'consulted' on tax calculations. Let me update that. The idea is that you're responsible for doing the calculation, but you consult with finance if there are questions about the underlying data or assumptions.

That makes sense. One more thing on the RACI: for the 'data collection' step, I'm listed as responsible, but I'm not always the one collecting the data—departments are. Should I be 'accountable' and departments be 'responsible'?

Actually, I think the way it's set up is correct. You're responsible for coordinating the data collection—sending reminders, following up, etc. Departments are responsible for providing the data. But in RACI terms, you're the one accountable if data doesn't arrive on time. Does that distinction make sense?
Yes, that makes sense. I'm accountable for the process, even if departments are doing the actual work. Got it.

On the reminder schedule, T-14, T-7, and T-3 days sounds reasonable. But I'm wondering if we should also have a reminder for the person assigned to submit the document, not just the department owner. Sometimes the owner doesn't pass the message along.

Good point. Yes, we should send reminders to both the department owner and the assigned individual. That way there's no excuse for missing a deadline. I'll update the reminder plan to include both contacts.
One more thing: what happens if a department misses the T-3 day deadline and we escalate to their manager? Do we have a procedure for that, or is it just a heads-up?

Good question. I think the escalation should be a formal notification to the manager, copied to the finance manager, saying 'This document is overdue. Please prioritise.' If it's still not submitted by T-1 day, we escalate further to the head of accounting. But let me check with the finance manager on the exact escalation path. For now, let's confirm the reminder schedule and RACI, and I'll validate the escalation procedure separately.

That sounds reasonable. So to confirm: reminders go to both department owner and assigned individual at T-14, T-7, and T-3 days. Escalation to manager at T-3 if not submitted, and further escalation at T-1 if still not submitted. Agreed?

Yes, that's the plan. Let me also confirm the RACI matrix decision: we've updated the tax calculation step so finance is 'consulted', and we've clarified that I'm accountable for data collection coordination. Does everyone agree with the updated RACI?
Yes, the updated RACI looks good to me.
Agreed. I'm comfortable with the RACI and the reminder schedule.
Yes, looks good.

Perfect. So D5 and D6 are locked: RACI matrix approved with the updates, and reminder/escalation schedule confirmed. I'll document the escalation procedure and get it reviewed by the finance manager by EOD tomorrow. T4 and T9 should be complete by mid-week.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and debrief the pilot run of the new workflow.

messages.text:
Hi team. Now that we have the templates, tracker, and RACI locked down, I think we should run a pilot on one monthly tax filing to test everything before full rollout.

I'm proposing we use the next monthly filing cycle—that's in about 10 days. We'll process all documents using the new templates and tracker, and I'll log any issues or deviations we encounter. After the pilot, we'll have a debrief meeting to discuss what worked and what needs adjustment.

Does this timeline work for everyone?

Good idea. A pilot will help us catch issues before we roll out to everyone. I have one question: should we include all departments in the pilot, or just a subset? If we include everyone, we get more realistic feedback, but there's also more risk if something breaks.

I'd suggest we include all departments but with a safety net. We run the new process in parallel with the old process for this one cycle. That way, if something goes wrong, we still have the old data to fall back on.
That's a good safety approach. But it also means double work for one cycle. Is that realistic given our timeline?

It's extra work, but it's worth it for confidence. We have 21 days total, and the pilot is in 10 days. That gives us 11 days after the pilot to make adjustments before the quarterly filing deadline. I think we can manage it. Let's go with the parallel approach: all departments, new process in parallel with old process, and we log all issues.

Okay, so the pilot scope is: all departments, monthly filing cycle in 10 days, parallel processing with old and new workflows. I'll create an issue log to track any problems we encounter. What should I be looking for? Format issues? Missing fields? Timing problems?

All of the above. Also look for: unclear instructions, departments struggling with the templates, tracker access issues, and any steps that take longer than expected. Basically, anything that makes the process harder or slower than the old way. Log it in the incident log (A7) with details on what happened and how long it took to resolve.
I'll help coordinate with departments during the pilot. I can also collect feedback from them on what's working and what's not.
I can help with the tracker setup and troubleshooting if there are access or formula issues.

Thanks. So here's the plan: pilot runs for the next monthly cycle (10 days), all departments participate in parallel, I log issues in the incident log, and we debrief after the filing is complete. Based on the debrief, we'll adjust templates and guidelines (T8) before full rollout.

Exactly. And after we adjust based on pilot feedback, we'll also need to document the incident handling procedure (T12) so we know how to handle discrepancies going forward. But let's focus on the pilot first. So D7 is locked: we're running the pilot on the next monthly filing cycle with all departments in parallel. Agreed?
Agreed. I'll start setting up the parallel process and coordinating with departments.
Confirmed. I'll reach out to departments today to give them a heads-up.

Good. Once the pilot is complete and we've debriefed, we'll make adjustments to templates and guidelines (D8). I'll schedule the debrief meeting for the day after the filing is complete. That gives us time to review the incident log and make decisions on what to change.
Sounds good. I'll be ready to help with any tracker adjustments if needed.

Perfect. So to summarise: D7 is locked—pilot scope confirmed. D8 will be locked after the debrief. T7 starts today, and we'll have the debrief and adjustments (T8) done by day 15 of the project. That leaves us 6 days for final training and rollout.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate training sessions and final rollout communication.

messages.text:
Team, we're in the final stretch. The pilot is wrapping up, and we need to plan the training sessions and final rollout. I've drafted training slides (A6) that walk through the new workflow, templates, tracker, and responsibilities.

I'm proposing two training sessions: one for accounting and finance staff, and one for operations. Each session is 1 hour, and I'll cover the key changes, walk through the templates, and answer questions.

I'm thinking we schedule these for day 17 and 18 of the project, which gives us a few days before the quarterly filing deadline to address any last-minute questions. Does this timeline work?
That timeline works for me. I can help coordinate attendance and send out calendar invites. How many people are we expecting in each session?

I'm estimating about 15-20 people per session. Accounting and finance have about 12-15 staff, and operations has about 8-10. We'll record the sessions and share the slides afterwards for anyone who can't attend.
Good. I'll also prepare a quick-reference guide (A3) that people can print and keep at their desk. It'll have the key steps, template fields, and who to contact if they have questions.

That's helpful. I'm a bit concerned about the rollout timing though. We're training on day 17-18, and the quarterly filing deadline is day 21. That's only 3 days for people to get comfortable with the new process. What if there are issues?

That's a fair concern. But remember, we've already run the pilot, so we've worked out most of the kinks. The training is really just to make sure everyone understands the new process. And we'll have support available during the filing cycle—I'll be monitoring the tracker closely and can help troubleshoot if needed.
I can also be available during the filing cycle to help departments with questions. And we have the quick-reference guide and recorded training to fall back on.
I'll also be available for any tax-related questions during the filing. And if there are any issues with the templates or tracker, we can make quick adjustments.
Okay, that sounds manageable. So we have support in place. I feel better about the timeline now.

Good. So let me confirm the training plan: two sessions on day 17-18, one for accounting/finance and one for operations. Sessions are 1 hour each, recorded, and slides shared afterwards. Quick-reference guide available. Support team on standby during filing. Does everyone agree?
Agreed. I'll make sure the quick-reference guide is ready by day 16.
Confirmed. I'll send out calendar invites by day 15.

Perfect. Now, for the go-live date: I'm proposing we officially go live with the new workflow on day 19, right after the training sessions. That gives people a day to absorb the training before they start using the new process for the quarterly filing. The quarterly filing deadline is day 21, so we have a 2-day buffer. Does that work?
That's tight, but it should work. We've done the pilot, we have support in place, and people will have had training. I'm comfortable with day 19 as the go-live date.
Day 19 works for me. That gives us time to monitor the first filing cycle and make any final adjustments if needed.
Okay, day 19 is good.

Excellent. So D9 and D10 are locked: training dates confirmed (day 17-18), and go-live date confirmed (day 19). After the quarterly filing is complete, we'll compile the post-rollout compliance and effectiveness report (T10) to measure how well the new process is working. That report will be due by day 25, giving us a few days after the filing deadline to collect data and analyse results.
I'll start collecting data on submission times and error rates as soon as we go live. That'll make the report easier to compile.

Perfect. So to summarise the final stretch: day 15, pilot debrief and adjustments complete. Day 16, quick-reference guide ready. Day 17-18, training sessions. Day 19, go-live. Day 21, quarterly filing deadline. Day 25, post-rollout report complete. We'll also need to update the statutory books alignment (T11) to reflect the new workflow. I'll coordinate that with the accounting team.
